{{Quote|The Empire discontinued use of this droid model after one unit went crazy and clawed something like 300 colonists on Corva Yag (out near Minos Cluster, I think).|Drev, Cynabar's Droid Datalog|<ref name="Journal13">{{JournalCite|13|Cynabar's Droid Datalog (article series)}}</ref>}}
'''Corva Yag''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]]. By [[214 BBY]], the [[Hajara gang]] of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] established a presence on Corva Yag, raiding [[Kett Shipping]] [[Convoy/Legends|convoys]] traveling across the [[Little Minos Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]].

Later, during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], several hundred [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] on Corva Yag [[Death/Legends|died]]. Their deaths were ostensibly caused by a malfunctioning [[87-RM Scout Collector]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]], although it was theorized by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] that the Empire had merely used the malfunctioning droid to cover up secret activities on the planet.

==Description==
Corva Yag was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="FF" /> located in the [[Corva Yag system/Legends|Corva Yag system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
{{Quote|For a couple of years Findal ran convoys across the Little Minos Run instead, but then the Hajara gang showed up on Corva Yag and started taking transports there.|Memoirs of Firmus Kett|<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-6-showdown-at-naboo|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 6: Showdown at Naboo}}</ref>}}
At some point by [[214 BBY]], [[Kett Shipping]] began running [[Ore/Legends|ore]] and [[Nova crystal/Legends|nova crystal]] [[Convoy/Legends|convoys]] across the [[Little Minos Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] in order to avoid the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]]-plagued [[Sanrafsix Corridor]] route. A few [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, however, the [[Hajara gang]] of pirates established a presence on Corva Yag and began raiding the company's [[Transport/Legends|transports]]. Eventually, the [[Trade Defense Force]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] dealt a blow to the Hajara gang, and Corva Yag was later mentioned in the memoirs of the Trade Defense Force [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Firmus Kett]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

[[File:87RM2-FF90.png|thumb|right|230px|It was rumored that a malfunctioning 87-RM Scout Collector droid caused the deaths of several hundred colonists on Corva Yag.]]
Rumors began circulating through [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="FF" /> by [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]<ref name="0 ABY">In {{JournalCite|13|Cynabar's Droid Datalog (article series)}}, the [[87-RM Scout Collector]] incident on Corva Yag is discussed [[in-universe]] by the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] 35:6:17, which corresponds to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> that a malfunctioning [[87-RM Scout Collector]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] had caused the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of several hundred [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] on Corva Yag.<ref name="FF" /> On the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] 35:6:17, [[Drev (Cynabar's Droid Datalog)|Drev]] claimed in an entry of [[Cynabar's Droid Datalog]] that the droid had [[Grasper arm/Legends|clawed]] approximately 300 people and that the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] had discontinued the use of the droid afterward. [[Thanik]] added on 35:8:1:04 that a public safety brief had been issued that named inserted counter-[[Programmer/Legends|programming]] as the cause for the droid's malfunction.<ref name="Journal13" />

On 35:9:1:8,<ref name="Journal13" /> the droid inventor and [[Historian/Legends|historian]]<ref name="Journal10">{{JournalCite|10|Toria Tell's Droid Journal (article)}}</ref> [[Toria Tell]] further speculated in the [[Datalog/Legends|datalog]] that the malfunction may have been caused by Imperial testing of new [[Weapon/Legends|weapon]] or droid programming protocols, or that the colonists had discovered a secret installation on Corva Yag, such as a hidden base or staging area, and had been silenced for it.<ref name="Journal13" /> Eventually, many came to believe that the Empire had made up the rumor about the malfunctioning 87-RM droid in order to hide its secret activities.<ref name="FF" />

==Behind the scenes==
Corva Yag was first mentioned in the "[[Cynabar's Droid Datalog (article series)|Cynabar's Droid Datalog]]" feature of the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 13|thirteenth issue]] of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine, which was published in [[May]] [[1997]]. The article was authored by [[Drew Campbell]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]].<ref name="Journal13" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Corva Yag [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet itself, in grid square N-20.<ref name="TEA" />
